samples.summary: New model-layer contract (`''` means "clear this inline-style key") is recorded only in a code comment and the task file, not in any design doc. `docs-font-controls.md` is the canonical doc for the color/clear-formatting surface and already documents the sibling convention ("applyInlineStyle already removes attributes when their value is explicitly undefined", lines 239-242); this change adds a second, exported semantic rule (`normalizeStyleClears`, exported from both `src/index.ts` and `src/node.ts`) without folding a sentence into that doc. CONTRIBUTING.md:58-60 asks for the existing doc to be updated for non-trivial/data-model changes. Also nothing in `packages/docs/src/store/store.ts`'s `applyStyle` contract (line 76) states that `''` is now interpreted as a clear, which is what a future third DocStore implementation would need to know.

samples.summary: The clear-normalization is applied twice, once per store implementation (`block-helpers.applyInlineStyle` for the memory/cache path and `applyStyleInTree` for the CRDT path), rather than once at the `Doc.applyInlineStyle` / store-boundary seam. This matches the task plan's checklist, so it is a taste point, not a criterion miss — but it means any future DocStore (or any direct `store.applyStyle`/`applyStyles` caller in another package) has to remember the rule, and the invariant lives in two files instead of one.
samples.evidence: normalizeStyleClears called at packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:316 and packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1878; `applyStyles` (line 1734) relies on both call sites for the same guarantee.

samples.summary: With a collapsed caret, `applyStyleImpl` stores the raw picker payload into pending style (`pending.set({ ...getSelectionStyleImpl(), ...style }, ...)`), so pending can hold `backgroundColor: ''` and `getSelectionStyle`/`getRangeStyleSummary` layer that `''` back to the toolbar until the pending style is consumed. The stored document is correct (consumeForInsert goes through `doc.applyInlineStyle`, which now normalizes), so this is a read-path cosmetic residue of the same two-values-mean-none problem the issue describes, not an acceptance-criterion miss.

verdict.reason: The absence is real and I verified it myself. `normalizeStyleClears` and the "`''` means clear this inline-style key" contract appear only in code (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:259-285), its re-exports (src/node.ts:73, src/index.ts), call sites (store/block-helpers.ts:3, frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts), tests (test/model/types.test.ts:115-137) and the task file (docs/tasks/active/20260817-docs-highlight-none-clear-todo.md:30-32). No design doc records it: docs-font-controls.md:229-242 documents only the sibling `undefined`-means-clear convention; greps across docs/design for `normalizeStyleClears`, `backgroundColor`, `empty string`/`''`, `applyStyle`, `removeStyleByPath`, `#793` turn up nothing about empty-string clears. I also chased indirect hops for a counterexample — packages/docs/README.md (no relevant matches), the canonical `DocStore.applyStyle` contract JSDoc (store/store.ts:75-81, says only "Apply inline style to a character range within a block."), and the InlineStyle/store-op contract in docs/design/docs/docs.md:96-129 — all silent. CONTRIBUTING.md:57-61 requires the existing area doc to be updated for architecture/data-model changes, and this adds an exported, cross-package interpretation rule for every applyStyle payload, which is this lens's named "design-doc discipline" major category. Caveat recorded, not used to refute: CONTRIBUTING.md:44-51 gives bug fixes a doc-free path and this is framed as a fix for #793, so a maintainer could class it as trivial; that is a judgement about requiredness, not a counterexample.
